query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled thermomechanical processing route that refines the microstructure (reducing grain size and healing processing‐induced flaws) will improve the integrity of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 by enhancing its resistance to crack propagation without reducing its inherent caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy that exhibits a large caloric response but suffers from poor fracture integrity and cracking.
generation.intervention: Apply severe plastic deformation (e.g., high-pressure torsion or equal-channel angular pressing) followed by a carefully optimized annealing treatment to achieve a uniform, ultrafine-grained microstructure with minimal processing defects.
generation.conditions: The thermomechanical processing is carried out at moderate-to-high pressures (in the SPD step) and followed by an annealing treatment in an inert atmosphere at a temperature selected to balance recrystallization with retention of the caloric phase (e.g., near but below the transformation temperature). Subsequent caloric tests are performed under the same applied-field and pressure conditions as used in prior studies (ambient to moderate elevated temperatures, controlled magnetic/pressure fields, and standard strain rates for mechanical testing).
generation.structural_mediator: A refined grain structure with reduced defect/flaw sizes and improved grain boundary cohesion.
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement increases the barrier to crack initiation and growth by reducing flaw sizes and promoting more uniform stress distribution. Because the intrinsic transformation mechanism that gives rise to the caloric response is maintained at the atomic scale, the ultrafine-grained microstructure improves mechanical integrity without altering the phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: The processed alloy should exhibit significantly higher compressive strength and fracture toughness (an increase relative to the crack-prone baseline) while retaining a caloric response comparable in magnitude (directionally unchanged) to that observed in the unprocessed material.
generation.baseline: The original cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with its known high caloric performance but poor mechanical integrity.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies under the same operational regimes of applied field and pressure (e.g., ambient/near-transformation temperatures, standard magnetic or pressure fields, and typical mechanical loading rates) where the caloric effect is normally measured.
generation.uncertainty: There is some uncertainty as to the optimal SPD and annealing parameters that will refine the grain structure sufficiently without triggering unwanted recrystallization or affecting the transformation behavior; experimental tuning is required.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 samples: one processed via the proposed severe plastic deformation followed by optimized annealing, and a control group as traditionally cast. Characterize both sets using electron microscopy to assess grain size and defect distribution. Then, measure compressive strength, fracture toughness, and caloric response (e.g., via differential scanning calorimetry under applied magnetic/pressure fields) under identical testing conditions.
measurements: Grain size distribution and defect density via electron microscopy
Compressive strength and fracture toughness via mechanical testing
Caloric performance (heat flow, transformation temperatures, entropy change) via calorimetric measurements under applied fields
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SPD‐annealed samples do not show an improvement in mechanical integrity (i.e., similar or lower compressive strength/fracture toughness) compared to the control, or if the caloric response is significantly diminished relative to the baseline performance, then the hypothesis is falsified.
